title: docs(comments): re-scope the #8959 CBP residue note to what #9138 actually closed
body:
Fixes #13722

Comments only, one paragraph, one file. Final commit `1d1263f26`.

## The false sentence

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` — the `[#8959]` paragraph at the `controlled_by_parent` stand-down site in `assertControlledByParentWrite` — said the #8772 ramp has "two code legs and **neither has landed yet**", and that #9138 "is dispatchable now but not yet merged".

Located by symbol and text, never by line number: the card cites `:6351-6367`, and after #14049 (`09e4b0ece`) landed upstream in the same file the paragraph is at `:6484-6500`. Anchored on the literal string `neither has landed yet`.

## Falsified before rewriting — and the card's suggested rewrite did not survive intact

Read directly from the API rather than from the card's paraphrase:

| | state today | reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| #9138 (Direction 2, builder force) | **closed / completed** `2026-08-17`, PR #9206 | the "neither has landed" sentence is false |
| #9139 (Direction 1, lint promotion) | **open**, `pm:on-hold`, `target:v18` | that half of the sentence is still true |

The card then proposed re-scoping the residue claim "to the raw `.parse()` path". **Measured against today's code, that would have replaced one false sentence with another.** It is true for one of the three residue shapes and false for the other two.

`forceCbpMasterDetailRequired` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`) returns early on `required === true` and never inspects `readonly` / `system`. So the two provenance-flagged shapes are still newly authorable through `ObjectSchema.create()` itself — not merely through raw parse. Measured by running the built `dist` of `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint`:

```
===== A. builder path: ObjectSchema.create() =====
M1   CBP + master_detail, `required` OMITTED          -> ok=true required=true   (forced)
M1c  CONTROL same shape, sharingModel private          -> ok=true required=false  (not forced)
M2   CBP + master_detail + `required: false`           -> ok=false  (refused, located error)
M2c  CONTROL same shape, sharingModel private          -> ok=true required=false  (accepted)
M3   CBP + master_detail + required:true + READONLY    -> ok=true  ACCEPTED
M4   CBP + master_detail + required:true + SYSTEM      -> ok=true  ACCEPTED
M5   CBP + master_detail + READONLY, required OMITTED  -> ok=true required=true readonly=true
M5b  CBP + master_detail + SYSTEM,   required OMITTED  -> ok=true required=true system=true

===== B. raw parse path: ObjectSchema.safeParse() =====
M6   safeParse CBP + `required: false`   -> success=true  required=false
M7   safeParse CBP + required OMITTED    -> success=true  required=false   (not forced at parse)
M7c  CONTROL safeParse with alias `isRequired` -> success=false unrecognized_keys@fields.order_id

===== C. lint relationship/master-detail-required =====
M8   required OMITTED            -> ["warning"]   | also fired: delete-behavior, line-items-inline-edit
M9   required:true + READONLY    -> []            | also fired: delete-behavior, line-items-inline-edit
M10  required:true + SYSTEM      -> []            | also fired: delete-behavior, line-items-inline-edit
M11  required:false              -> ["warning"]   | also fired: delete-behavior, line-items-inline-edit
```

Every zero above is a reading, not an absence:

- **M9 / M10** report no `master-detail-required` finding, and in the *same* lint call two other rules do fire — so the linter is live on that object and the zero is about the predicate, which is still `def.required !== true` at `severity: 'warning'`.
- **M7c** is the control for the parse leg: the same `safeParse` refuses an alias key, so M6/M7's `success=true` is a decision and not a comparator that always says yes.
- **M1c / M2c** are the controls for the builder leg: the same shapes under `sharingModel: 'private'` are *not* forced and *not* refused, so the force is CBP-scoped rather than unconditional.

M5 / M5b are the sharpest reading: the force **mints** the two flagged shapes. A `readonly` or `system` master reference authored with `required` omitted comes out of `create()` as `required: true` plus the flag — which is exactly a shape `validateRecord` skips (`if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;`), leaving the security gate the sole refusal. That matches `omissionRefusedByValidation`'s own predicate, `def?.type === 'master_detail' && !!def?.required && !def?.readonly && !def?.system`.

The rewritten paragraph states all of that, plus the parts of the old text that re-measured true (#8772 ruled; #9139 held for v18; `main` still 17.x — `packages/spec` is `17.2.0`).

## The non-comment diff is empty — with a live comparator

Both versions transpiled with `removeComments: true` and compared two independent ways (output text and `ts.createScanner` token stream), plus two controls:

```
raw byte lengths: BASE=398918  WORKING=400382  (raw sources differ: true)

### SUBJECT - BASE vs WORKING TREE (this PR diff)
  stripped-TEXT : A sha=ee8e85d25ba0ae6b (136185 B)  B sha=ee8e85d25ba0ae6b (136185 B)  -> IDENTICAL
  TOKEN stream  : A n=11864 sha=799a1855bdacd000  B n=11864 sha=799a1855bdacd000  -> IDENTICAL

### REVERSE CONTROL - WORKING TREE + one-token CODE change ('insert' -> 'update')
  stripped-TEXT : ... -> DIFFERENT   first diff line 2241
  TOKEN stream  : ... -> DIFFERENT   first diff index 10817: A="11:'insert'" B="11:'update'"

### CONTROL 2 - WORKING TREE + comment-TEXT change
  stripped-TEXT : -> IDENTICAL
  TOKEN stream  : -> IDENTICAL

subject non-comment diff EMPTY     : true
reverse control reports NON-empty  : true
comment-only control reports EMPTY : true
OVERALL: PASS
```

Exit code captured before any pipe: `node noncomment-diff.cjs ... ; echo "EXIT=$?"` gave `0`. An earlier run exited **9** because control 2's anchor matched 0 times — reported as NOT RUN, not as a pass; the anchor was fixed and the control then actually ran.

## Gates

Re-derived from the actual diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no path arguments — the script took the change set from the merge base itself), both output sections read whole. 21 matched families plus 2 convention-triggered i18n families. All run at `1d1263f26`:

- **22 PASS** — including `check:comment-mask-adoption`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:keyed-text-bounds`, `check:system-context-census` (whose declared population is literally this file), `check:tenant-audit-census`, `check:published-files`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:nul-bytes`, and `check:i18n-stale-fill`.
- `pnpm check:i18n` first exited 1 with its own verdict line reading `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace CLI is not built` / "Nothing was checked". Not recorded as a red: the named build closure was run and the gate then **passed**, reporting `plugins/plugin-security  in sync (7 bundle(s))` and `OK (9 package(s))`.
- **2 NOT MEASURED**, both exit 3, neither a pass and neither a red:
  - `check-test-completeness` — grades a saved `turbo run test` log; the gate's own text says to record the local reading as NOT MEASURED. CI supplies the log.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — needs a full `pnpm build`; still reports missing `dist/` for ~73 packages after the i18n closure. CI runs it.

Beyond the family: `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) run repo-wide in the foreground, **exit 0, 5623 files linted, 0 findings** — and this PR's file is confirmed present in that population at `errors=0 warnings=0`, so the zero is a measurement rather than a file eslint never opened. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck` exit 0 (it runs `tsconfig.test.json` too). `@objectstack/plugin-security` vitest: **94 files / 1764 tests passed**.

No changeset: comments-only, publishes nothing. Same disposition as #14049, the reference PR for this shape, which carried `skip-changeset` for a diff that included this same file.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

#14130 — the adjacent `[#9137]` freeze note cites `record-validator.ts:993 / :1003` for the provenance skip; both anchors have rotted (the guard is at `:1037` / `:1047`, and `:993`/`:1003` land on unrelated docblock prose while still being in range). Filed unassigned rather than folded in, because #13722's ruling fences this card to the one paragraph. Same class as #13556, different carrier.

The repo-wide sweep of similar stale comments is not addressed here; that surface belongs to #14046, which stays open.
